blogs.title: Agentic AI for Indian Enterprises: Use Cases, Architecture and Deployment Guide (2026)
blogs.summary: Defines agentic AI as goal-driven, multi-step, tool-using systems with memory and guardrails. Five use cases: government tender analysis, automobile warranty claims, agri-finance loan files, manufacturing quality incident reports, and enterprise Q&A that takes action. Design rules: define the agent's authority boundary, add human checkpoints, log every action. States their agentic framework on ADVIT keeps boundaries in configuration, has workflow interruption points and immutable audit logs.

blogs.title: LLMOps for Indian Enterprises: The Production Deployment Guide (2026)
blogs.summary: Explains the gap between an LLM demo and production. Six pillars: prompt versioning, model lifecycle management, fine-tuning and RAG pipeline management, evaluation and quality monitoring, cost and latency optimisation, security and governance. Argues on-premise, hardware-agnostic LLMOps suits DPDP-regulated Indian sectors.

faq_from_site_content.a: Automaton AI's platform for the full deep learning and LLM lifecycle: data labeling, feature engineering, training, deployment and monitoring, on-premise or cloud.

faq_from_site_content.q: Can it run on-premise or air-gapped?
faq_from_site_content.a: Yes. Automaton AI states on-premise is the default and air-gapped deployment is supported for defence and government.
PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, TensorRT, Hugging Face and JAX on the current page; older pages also list Keras and Darknet.
Bounding box, semantic segmentation, key point, text, polygon, lines and splines, cuboid and 3D point cloud.

faq_from_site_content.q: Does Automaton AI offer managed labeling?
faq_from_site_content.a: Yes: data collection, annotation workforce, multi-layer QA and delivery in any requested format.

The discipline of managing the full lifecycle of LLM systems in production, including prompt versioning, model registry, RAG pipelines, evaluation, cost control and governance. It differs from MLOps because LLMs are non-deterministic and sensitive to prompt and vendor model changes.

faq_from_site_content.q: How long does an LLMOps or agentic deployment take?
faq_from_site_content.a: Automaton AI's blog estimates 4-6 weeks for a foundational LLMOps setup, 3-4 months for full maturity, 3-4 weeks for a single-workflow agentic system and 2-3 months for multi-workflow agent systems. These are estimates, not commitments.
Pricing is not published. Use the Connect form and choose Explore pricing for ADVIT Studio, or email info@automatonai.com.

faq_from_site_content.q: How do I book a demo?
faq_from_site_content.a: Use the Connect form (Schedule a demo) or the homepage form (Demo). The V2 page says a pilot can be scoped in under 2 weeks.
